translation.text: As for your cry, cry out for judgment, and it will appear to you,[a] because all your suffering will be required of the angels and of all those who helped those who drive you away.[b]

footnotes.text: The opening joins “your cry,” judgment, and the command to cry out. The following verb can mean “appear” or “become manifest”; its precise subject is not expressed. “It” is understood here as the requested judgment, but the Ge’ez does not explicitly name the appearing subject. The word is not limited to the sense “cause something else to appear.”
The selected edition prints “angels” here. This is the wording of the edited text, not a substitution of rulers or a claim that independent manuscripts have been checked.

proposed_final_wording.text: Because you sinners say, “You are not called to account, and all our sins are not written down”—all your sins are being written down every day.[a]

footnotes.text: The selected Ge’ez shifts from addressing “you sinners” to the second-person “you are not called to account,” then to “our sins” inside the saying, and back to “your sins.” These person shifts are retained rather than silently replacing the second person with “we.” The following assertion contradicts the sinners’ denial.

translation.text: In those days the Lord said, “They will call and announce to the children of the earth through their wisdom. Show them that you are their guides, and show them a reward over the whole earth.”[a]

footnotes.text: The selected edition shifts from third-person plural “they will call” and “make hear” to the plural command “show them.” The final “reward” phrase is compressed. This rendering understands it as another object of “show them,” supplying that verb a second time in English; the Ge’ez does not repeat it. Another possible attachment would link reward with the description of the addressees, but that is not stated as certain.

proposed_correction.basis: Retain printed third/secondperson shift. Avoid unexpressed reflexiveobject; accusative reward can depend on showthem. Proposed supplied verb is disclosed, not claimed as repeated in Ge’ez.
